---
title: Source maps and local overrides
description: A source map links each position in the shipped bundle back to your original file, and a local override lets you test a changed response without a deploy.
order: 4
concepts: [source map, base64 VLQ, sourceMappingURL, local overrides, fetch and XHR override]

{/* <!-- concept: source-maps --> */}

Your build tool minifies `src` files into one bundle, `app.min.js`. The browser runs that bundle, so breakpoints and errors point at unreadable code. A **source map** is a JSON file that links each position in the generated code back to a position in an original file. With it, DevTools shows your own files.

{/* <!-- concept: source-map-vlq-mappings --> */}

The generated file names its map in a `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment. The map lists the original files in `sources` and positions in `mappings`. A `;` ends a generated line, a `,` separates segments, and each segment holds numbers in **base64 VLQ** (variable-length quantity), a compact number code.

<PredictReveal
  prompt="DevTools pauses on the second line of app.min.js. The map file returns 404, or JavaScript source maps are off in Settings. What does the Sources panel show?"
  options={["Your original src file at the right line", "The minified app.min.js with short names", "An error, and the page stops running"]}
  correct={1}
  answer="It shows the minified app.min.js, and the call stack points into the bundle."
  reasoning="DevTools finds the original file only through the map. Without the map, nothing links the generated position to an original file, so DevTools shows the code the browser runs. The map is for tools; the page runs the same without it."
/>

Follow one lookup from left to right.

<Diagram id="source-map-lookup" />

`A` is 0, `C` is +1 and `D` is −1. DevTools adds each change to the previous segment, so the position lands on line index 1 of `sources[0]`. You pay with an extra file per bundle.

{/* <!-- concept: local-overrides --> */}

{/* <!-- concept: override-xhr-fetch --> */}

**Local overrides** save your edit of a served response to a folder on your disk, for any site. On reload, DevTools serves the saved copy instead of the network response. You can also override a fetch or XHR response. You test a fix or a new API shape without a deploy. You cannot override a source-mapped file.

A **workspace** connects your own project folder to DevTools instead. Edit a CSS, HTML or JavaScript file in Sources, save, and DevTools writes the change to the source file on your disk. Use it to keep a fix in your real code. DevTools does not save DOM edits from the Elements panel.

<Depth level="internals">

VLQ letters `A` to `Z` and `a` to `f` end a number; `g` to `z`, digits, `+` and `/` mean another letter follows. The lowest bit of the joined value is the sign, so `D` (3) is −1. A segment has 1, 4 or 5 fields: generated column, source index, original line, original column, and an optional name index. The generated column resets at each `;`; the other fields carry over across the whole map. DevTools decodes `mappings` only at the first lookup and rejects values over 32 bits (`front_end/core/sdk/SourceMap.ts:472-496 @ 572bfc0`).

</Depth>

<Depth level="production">

When both a comment and a `sourcemap` header exist, the header wins. A map with `sourcesContent` embeds your original text, so treat it like source code. Build tools can set `ignoreList` to mark framework and bundler files, and DevTools can hide those frames from stepping and the call stack. Chrome still reads the older `x_google_ignoreList` when `ignoreList` is absent (`front_end/core/sdk/SourceMap.ts:551 @ 572bfc0`).

</Depth>
